name: Standard antenatal care (FOGSI / WHO / Government of India) – DRAFT
description: Combined antenatal schedule drafted from WHO 2016, Government of India (MoHFW) and FOGSI guidance. Must be reviewed and approved by a doctor before use.
sources: WHO ANC recommendations 2016; MoHFW (Government of India) ANC, GDM and Anemia Mukt Bharat guidance; FOGSI good clinical practice recommendations.

items.name: Booking visit (registration, history, examination)
items.source: WHO: first contact by 12 weeks; MoHFW: first visit as early as possible, before 12 weeks

items.name: Antenatal visit (16 weeks)
items.source: FOGSI/Indian practice: 4-weekly visits in the second trimester

items.name: Antenatal visit (20 weeks)
items.source: WHO contact 2 (20 weeks)

items.name: Antenatal visit (24–26 weeks)
items.source: WHO contact 3 (26 weeks); MoHFW visit 2 (14–26 weeks)

items.name: Antenatal visit (28–30 weeks)
items.source: WHO contact 4 (30 weeks); MoHFW visit 3 (28–34 weeks)

items.name: Antenatal visit (32 weeks)
items.source: FOGSI/Indian practice: 2-weekly visits from 28 to 36 weeks

items.name: Antenatal visit (34 weeks)
items.source: WHO contact 5 (34 weeks)

items.name: Antenatal visit (36 weeks)
items.source: WHO contact 6 (36 weeks); MoHFW visit 4 (36 weeks–term)

items.name: Antenatal visit (37 weeks)
items.source: FOGSI/Indian practice: weekly visits from 36 weeks

items.name: Antenatal visit (38 weeks)
items.source: WHO contact 7 (38 weeks)

items.name: Antenatal visit (39 weeks)
items.source: FOGSI/Indian practice: weekly visits from 36 weeks

items.name: Antenatal visit (40 weeks) – plan for delivery
items.source: WHO contact 8 (40 weeks)

items.name: Post-dates assessment (41 weeks) if not delivered
items.patientText: Check-up at 41 weeks if baby not yet born
items.source: Common practice: review for induction at 41 weeks – doctor to confirm

items.name: Complete blood count (Hb)
items.source: MoHFW / Anemia Mukt Bharat: Hb at first visit

items.name: Blood group and Rh typing
items.source: WHO, MoHFW, FOGSI

items.name: Urine routine and microscopy (protein, sugar)
items.source: MoHFW; urine protein at every visit

items.name: GDM screening: 75 g OGTT (2-hour plasma glucose)
items.source: MoHFW GDM guidelines: universal screening at first visit

items.name: HIV test (with counselling)
items.source: MoHFW / NACO: universal antenatal HIV testing

items.name: Syphilis test (VDRL / RPR)
items.source: WHO, MoHFW

items.name: Hepatitis B (HBsAg)
items.source: FOGSI / MoHFW

items.name: Thyroid test (TSH)
items.source: FOGSI: universal thyroid screening in pregnancy recommended in India – doctor to confirm

items.name: Indirect Coombs test (ICT)
items.source: FOGSI: ICT for Rh-negative mothers at booking

items.name: GDM screening: repeat 75 g OGTT
items.source: MoHFW GDM guidelines: repeat at 24–28 weeks if first test normal

items.name: Repeat haemoglobin
items.source: MoHFW: Hb in each trimester

items.name: Repeat indirect Coombs test (ICT)
items.source: FOGSI: repeat ICT at 28 weeks before anti-D

items.name: Haemoglobin and urine before delivery
items.patientText: Blood and urine tests before delivery
items.source: Common practice before delivery – doctor to confirm

items.name: Dating / viability scan
items.source: FOGSI / common practice: first-trimester dating scan

items.name: NT scan with first-trimester combined screening (double marker)
items.patientText: Ultrasound and blood test for baby’s health (11–13 weeks)
items.source: FOGSI: combined first-trimester screening at 11–13+6 weeks

items.name: Anomaly scan (level II / TIFFA)
items.source: FOGSI / WHO: one ultrasound before 24 weeks; 18–20 weeks usual in India

items.name: Growth scan
items.source: Common Indian practice – doctor to decide if routine or only when indicated

items.name: Growth scan with Doppler
items.source: For high-risk pregnancies – doctor to confirm indications and timing

items.name: Growth scan (twins, separate placentas) – 24 weeks
items.source: NICE NG137 (2019) / ISUOG twin guideline: dichorionic twins – growth scan at least every 4 weeks from 24 weeks; monochorionic twins need a scan every 2 weeks from 16 weeks (add them for her) – doctor to confirm

items.name: Growth scan (twins, separate placentas) – 28 weeks
items.source: NICE NG137 (2019) / ISUOG twin guideline: dichorionic twins – growth scan at least every 4 weeks – doctor to confirm

items.name: Growth scan with amniotic fluid (gestational diabetes)
items.patientText: Ultrasound to check baby’s growth (28–30 weeks)
items.source: MoHFW GDM guidelines (2018): growth scan at 28–30 weeks for GDM, repeated at 34–36 weeks – doctor to confirm

items.name: Growth scan (twins, separate placentas) – 32 weeks
items.source: NICE NG137 (2019) / ISUOG twin guideline: dichorionic twins – growth scan at least every 4 weeks. It takes the place of the routine growth scan at 30–32 weeks (mark that one not needed); the 36-week scan is the high-risk growth scan – doctor to confirm

items.name: Repeat scan for the position of the placenta
items.source: RCOG Green-top 27a (2018): follow-up scan at 32 weeks for a low-lying placenta or praevia; if it is still low, again at 36 weeks – doctor to confirm

items.name: Td (tetanus-diphtheria) – dose 1 (or booster)
items.source: MoHFW UIP: Td-1 early in pregnancy; single booster if vaccinated in last 3 years

items.name: Td – dose 2
items.source: MoHFW UIP: Td-2 four weeks after Td-1 (not needed if booster given)

items.name: Tdap (whooping cough protection)
items.patientText: Tdap injection (protects baby from whooping cough)
items.source: FOGSI: Tdap at 27–36 weeks – may replace Td-2 in private practice; doctor to decide

items.name: Inactivated influenza vaccine (in flu season)
items.source: FOGSI / WHO: influenza vaccine in any trimester during flu season – doctor to decide

items.name: Anti-D immunoglobulin (if ICT negative)
items.source: FOGSI: antenatal anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks for Rh-negative, ICT-negative mothers

items.name: Folic acid 400 mcg daily (until 12 weeks)
items.patientText: Folic acid tablet every day until 3 months
items.source: WHO / MoHFW

items.name: Iron-folic acid daily from 14 weeks (at least 180 days)
items.patientText: Iron tablet every day from 4th month
items.source: MoHFW / Anemia Mukt Bharat

items.name: Calcium 500 mg twice daily from 14 weeks
items.source: MoHFW calcium supplementation guidance

items.name: Albendazole 400 mg single dose (second trimester)
items.source: MoHFW: deworming in the second trimester

items.name: Nutrition, rest and hygiene counselling
items.patientText: Eat a balanced diet, rest well, and keep taking your tablets
items.source: WHO / MoHFW

items.name: Danger signs counselling
items.patientText: Come to hospital at once for bleeding, severe headache, blurred vision, fits, fever, leaking water or reduced baby movements
items.source: WHO / MoHFW

items.name: Fetal movement counting
items.patientText: Count your baby’s movements every day
items.source: Common practice from 28 weeks

items.name: Birth preparedness and breastfeeding counselling
items.patientText: Plan for delivery; learn about breastfeeding
items.source: WHO / MoHFW birth preparedness

items.name: Twins or more: check the number of placentas – a shared placenta (monochorionic) or triplets need more scans (add them for her)
items.patientText: Ask your doctor how often you need an ultrasound scan
items.source: NICE NG137 (2019) / ISUOG twin guideline: chorionicity is decided at the 11–14 week scan. Monochorionic twins: a scan every 2 weeks from 16 weeks; triplets: every 2 weeks (from 16 weeks when a placenta is shared). The built-in twin scans at 24, 28 and 32 weeks are for dichorionic twins only – doctor to confirm

name: Standard postnatal care (WHO / Government of India) – DRAFT
description: Postnatal schedule for the mother, counted from the day of delivery. Must be reviewed and approved by a doctor before use.
sources: WHO postnatal care recommendations 2022; MoHFW Home-Based Postnatal Care; Anemia Mukt Bharat.

items.name: Postnatal check within 24 hours (bleeding, BP, breastfeeding)
items.patientText: Check-up on the day after delivery
items.source: WHO 2022: first contact within 24 hours

items.name: Postnatal check (day 3)
items.source: WHO 2022 / MoHFW HBPNC: day 3

items.name: Postnatal check (days 7–14): wound or perineum, breastfeeding, mood
items.source: WHO 2022: between day 7 and 14

items.name: Caesarean wound check and stitch removal if needed (7–10 days)
items.patientText: Wound check about a week after the operation
items.source: Indian practice; doctor to confirm

items.name: Postnatal check (6 weeks): recovery, BP, contraception
items.source: WHO 2022 / MoHFW: 6 weeks

items.name: Haemoglobin (anaemia check)
items.patientText: Blood test for haemoglobin at 6 weeks
items.source: Anemia Mukt Bharat

items.name: BP check within the first week (hypertension)
items.patientText: Blood pressure check in the first week
items.source: WHO 2022; doctor to confirm for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy

items.name: Blood sugar review (diabetes)
items.source: MoHFW GDM guidance: 75 g OGTT 6–12 weeks after delivery after GDM; doctor to confirm

items.name: Anti-D within 72 hours (Rh-negative mother, Rh-positive baby)
items.source: Standard practice; doctor to confirm the baby’s blood group

items.name: Iron and folic acid daily for 6 months
items.patientText: Iron tablets every day for 6 months
items.source: Anemia Mukt Bharat

items.name: Calcium daily for 6 months
items.patientText: Calcium tablets every day for 6 months
items.source: MoHFW

items.name: Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months
items.patientText: Give only breast milk for the first 6 months
items.source: WHO / MoHFW

items.name: Danger signs (heavy bleeding, fever, foul discharge, severe headache, breathlessness)
items.patientText: Come at once for heavy bleeding, fever, bad-smelling discharge, severe headache or breathlessness
items.source: WHO 2022

items.name: Family planning counselling (PPIUCD, other methods)
items.source: MoHFW postpartum family planning

name: Newborn care and immunisation (Government of India UIP) – DRAFT
description: Newborn checks and the national immunisation schedule, counted from the day of birth. Must be reviewed and approved by a doctor before use.
sources: Government of India Universal Immunization Programme schedule; WHO newborn care; MoHFW Home-Based Newborn Care.

items.name: Newborn examination within 24 hours
items.source: WHO / MoHFW

items.name: Newborn check (days 3–7): weight, jaundice, feeding, cord
items.patientText: Baby check-up in the first week
items.source: MoHFW HBNC

items.name: Newborn screening (heel prick) after 48 hours: hypothyroidism, G6PD, CAH, galactosaemia, PKU, biotinidase
items.patientText: Heel-prick blood test for the baby (after 2 days of age)
items.source: MoHFW RBSK newborn screening

items.name: Pulse-oximetry heart screen (CCHD) after 24 hours, before going home
items.patientText: Oxygen check on the baby's hand and foot
items.source: AAP / AHA critical congenital heart disease screening

items.name: Hearing screen (OAE) before going home, or by 1 month
items.source: MoHFW RBSK; JCIH 1-3-6 (screen by 1 month)

items.name: Birth doses: BCG, OPV-0, Hepatitis B (birth dose)
items.patientText: Vaccines at birth: BCG, polio drops, Hepatitis B
items.source: UIP: at birth (Hep B within 24 hours)

items.name: 6 weeks: OPV-1, Pentavalent-1, Rotavirus-1, fIPV-1, PCV-1
items.source: UIP

items.name: 10 weeks: OPV-2, Pentavalent-2, Rotavirus-2
items.source: UIP

items.name: 14 weeks: OPV-3, Pentavalent-3, Rotavirus-3, fIPV-2, PCV-2
items.source: UIP

items.name: 9 months: MR-1, PCV booster, fIPV-3, JE-1 (where endemic)
items.source: UIP (9–12 months)

items.name: Vitamin A, first dose (9 months)
items.source: UIP

items.name: 16–24 months: MR-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster, JE-2 (where endemic)
items.source: UIP

items.name: Vitamin A, second dose (16 months), then every 6 months till 5 years
items.patientText: Vitamin A every 6 months till 5 years
items.source: UIP

items.name: 5–6 years: DPT booster-2
items.source: UIP

items.name: 10 years: Td
items.source: UIP

items.name: 16 years: Td
items.source: UIP

items.name: Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months; keep warm; cord care
items.patientText: Only breast milk for 6 months, keep the baby warm, keep the cord dry
items.source: WHO / MoHFW

items.name: Danger signs (poor feeding, fast breathing, fever or cold, yellow skin, convulsions)
items.patientText: Come at once if the baby feeds poorly, breathes fast, is hot or cold, turns yellow or has fits
items.source: WHO IMNCI

items.source: Standard practice

items.name: Haemoglobin (anaemia screening)

items.name: Clinical breast examination
items.source: MoHFW screening of common cancers

items.name: Cervical cancer screening if due (VIA / Pap / HPV test; women 30–65)

items.name: Follow-up with reports
items.source: Standard practice

items.name: Annual gynaecology review
items.source: FOGSI

items.name: Repeat cervical screening (if the last result was normal)
items.source: Pap every 3 years / HPV every 5 years; doctor decides

name: Infertility evaluation (FOGSI / ICMR / NICE) – DRAFT
description: First evaluation of the couple, counted from the first fertility visit. Must be reviewed and approved by a doctor before use.
sources: ICMR national guidelines for infertility evaluation (2018); FOGSI; NICE CG156 Fertility problems.

items.name: Fertility consultation (history of both partners, examination)
items.patientText: First fertility check-up (please come with your partner)
items.source: ICMR / NICE

items.name: Folic acid daily while trying to conceive
items.source: NICE CG156 / WHO

items.name: Day 2–3 hormones: FSH, LH, AMH, TSH, prolactin
items.patientText: Blood tests on day 2–3 of the period
items.source: ICMR / FOGSI

items.name: Baseline transvaginal scan (antral follicle count, uterus, ovaries)
items.source: ICMR / FOGSI

items.name: Semen analysis (partner)
items.source: WHO 2021 laboratory manual; ICMR

items.name: Rubella immunity; HIV, HBsAg, HCV, VDRL (both partners)
items.source: NICE CG156 / ICMR

items.name: Tubal patency test (HSG / sono-HSG), days 6–10 of the cycle
items.source: ICMR / NICE

items.name: Review with all reports and treatment plan

items.source: Standard practice; doctor decides

name: Care after pregnancy loss (NICE / RCOG / FOGSI / ESHRE) – DRAFT
description: Follow-up after a miscarriage, an ectopic or a molar pregnancy, and the work-up for recurrent loss, counted from the day the loss was diagnosed (the date seen on the record). Which items apply follows the type of loss, its management, the anti-D answer and the Abortions (A) count on the record. Must be reviewed and approved by a doctor before use.
sources: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage (2019, updated 2023); RCOG Green-top Guideline 38 Gestational trophoblastic disease (2020) and 21 Ectopic pregnancy (2016); FOGSI / FIGO 2021 (trophoblastic disease); ESHRE Recurrent pregnancy loss (update 2022); WHO Medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use (2015); Anemia Mukt Bharat.

items.name: Follow-up visit 1–2 weeks after the loss: bleeding, pain, fever, how she is coping; the report of any tissue sent
items.source: Standard practice; doctor to confirm the interval

items.name: Haemoglobin (anaemia after blood loss)
items.source: Anemia Mukt Bharat; standard practice after blood loss

items.name: Anti-D for an Rh-negative woman, within 72 hours – record it under Pregnancy loss (Edit details)
items.source: NICE NG126: offer after surgical management of a miscarriage or an ectopic pregnancy; not after medical or expectant management alone, or a complete miscarriage. Many Indian units give it to every Rh-negative woman – doctor decides. The item stops applying once anti-D is recorded as given or not needed.

items.name: Contraception: ask what she wishes – fertility can return before the next period
items.source: WHO Medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use (2015): most methods can be started straight after a loss in the first 12 weeks; after a molar pregnancy see its own item. Doctor to confirm.

items.name: Next pregnancy: folic acid before trying, early booking; when to try again is for her and the doctor to decide (after methotrexate: wait at least 3 months)
items.patientText: Advice for planning your next pregnancy
items.source: WHO technical consultation on birth spacing (2005): 6 months after a miscarriage – later studies find no harm in conceiving sooner. RCOG Green-top Guideline 21 (2016): wait at least 3 months after methotrexate. Doctor to advise.

items.name: Beta hCG after molar pregnancy – every 2 weeks until normal (RCOG GTG 38): 2 weeks
items.source: RCOG Green-top Guideline 38 (2020): complete mole – follow up for 6 months from the evacuation if hCG is normal within 56 days, otherwise 6 months from the first normal value; partial mole – ends when hCG is normal on two samples at least 4 weeks apart. Every 2 weeks until normal: UK centres. FOGSI / FIGO 2021: every 1–2 weeks until normal, then monthly – how long varies. Doctor to confirm.

items.name: Beta hCG after molar pregnancy – every 2 weeks until normal (RCOG GTG 38): 4 weeks
items.source: RCOG Green-top Guideline 38 (2020): complete mole – follow up for 6 months from the evacuation if hCG is normal within 56 days, otherwise 6 months from the first normal value; partial mole – ends when hCG is normal on two samples at least 4 weeks apart. items.source: RCOG Green-top Guideline 38 (2020): complete mole – follow up for 6 months from the evacuation if hCG is normal within 56 days, otherwise 6 months from the first normal value; partial mole – ends when hCG is normal on two samples at least 4 weeks apart. items.source: RCOG Green-top Guideline 38 (2020): complete mole – follow up for 6 months from the evacuation if hCG is normal within 56 days, otherwise 6 months from the first normal value; partial mole – ends when hCG is normal on two samples at least 4 weeks apart. items.name: Molar pregnancy: no new pregnancy until hCG follow-up is complete; contraception – no intrauterine device until hCG is normal
items.patientText: Please avoid a new pregnancy until your doctor says the follow-up is complete
items.source: RCOG Green-top Guideline 38 (2020): no pregnancy until follow-up ends; RCOG has advised barrier methods until hCG is normal. WHO Medical eligibility criteria (2015): with hCG falling or undetectable, pills, injections and implants are category 1 and an intrauterine device category 3. The two differ – the doctor confirms the current advice.

items.name: Beta hCG, ectopic managed by waiting (NICE NG126): day 2
items.source: Waiting – NICE NG126 (2019, updated 2023): hCG days 2, 4, 7, then weekly until negative (under 20 IU/L) if it falls 15% or more each time. Methotrexate – NICE NG126 and RCOG GTG 21 (2016): days 4 and 7, then weekly until negative. After a salpingotomy (tube kept) NICE NG126 also advises hCG follow-up: include these items yourself. Move an item if day 0 was another day. Doctor to confirm.

items.name: Recurrent-loss work-up (the doctor decides when; ESHRE 2022 advises it after two losses): antiphospholipid antibodies, TSH and TPO antibodies, uterine anatomy
items.source: ESHRE Recurrent pregnancy loss (2022): antiphospholipid antibodies, thyroid tests and the uterus after two losses; parental karyotype and thrombophilia tests only after assessment. Applies from the number of losses set in the app, counted from Abortions (A) – which may include losses that were not spontaneous: the doctor confirms, and decides for each woman.
